sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know reported speech with *dijo que* and the tense shift from B1 Unit 13 (*dijo que no conocía*, *afirmó que había visto*, *dijo que hablaría*). History is often told this way: we paraphrase what a president declared, in our own words and without quotation marks. After a past verb such as *declaró* or *dijo*, the verb inside moves back.

sections.title: The tense moves back
rows: *no deben fundar* → *declaró que no debían fundar*

items.spanish: En 1823 el presidente Monroe declaró que los países europeos no debían fundar nuevas colonias en América.
items.english: In 1823 President Monroe declared that the European countries should not found new colonies in America.

items.spanish: Dijo también que Estados Unidos no intervendría en los asuntos de Europa.
items.english: He also said that the United States would not intervene in the affairs of Europe.

items.spanish: Roosevelt decía que Estados Unidos podía usar la fuerza militar si lo consideraba necesario.
items.english: Roosevelt said that the United States could use military force if it considered it necessary.

items.spanish: Algunos historiadores dijeron que la doctrina servía sobre todo a los intereses de Estados Unidos.
items.english: Some historians said that the doctrine served above all the interests of the United States.

sections.content: Use *que* after the reporting verb and move the tense back. Do not use quotation marks unless you are sure of the exact words: *declaró que…* reports the meaning, not the wording.
